If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), apply a 0.5% downward adjustment if price has trended upward recently, or upward if downward.  
For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is bullish, apply a 1–1.5% upward bias to reflect momentum; if bearish, apply a 1–1.5% downward bias to reflect risk-off behavior.  
If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in the following 5-day window to correct for sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00–0.33) over 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to reflect lack of conviction.
